description_full: Hutchison Port Holdings Trust invests in, develops, operates, and manages deep-water container ports in Guangdong Province of the People's Republic of China, Hong Kong, and Macau. The company invests in other types of port assets, such as river ports; and undertakes various port ancillary services, including trucking, feedering, freight forwarding, supply chain management, warehousing, and distribution services. Hutchison Port Holdings Trust was incorporated in 2011 and is based in Singapore.

financial_summary: Hutchison Port Holdings Trust is a mid-cap industrials business with a $2.2B market cap on $1.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -1% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.
Returns on capital run at 6% against a 7% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 39%.

The business throws off $571M in free cash flow — roughly 39 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 6.58× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.2× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 5.8×.

Management returns a meaningful 6.1% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 30% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 3.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
